title: Canonical exact-derived affine algebra counit is invertible
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $g:(X,\mathcal O_X)\to(Y,f_*\mathcal O_X)$ be its direct-image-algebra morphism [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. Assume the derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over both ringed spaces exist. Let $P:\operatorname{Mod}(f_*\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits, with an adjunction $a:P\dashv g_*$ to module direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. Let $b:D(P)\dashv Rg_*$ be the canonical derived adjunction induced by $a$, using termwise exact $P$ and the K-injective right-derived functor [lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived]. For every $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent in all integer degrees [def-pc-derived-category], the counit $b_K:D(P)(Rg_*K)\to K$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use exact scalar restriction from the direct-image algebra to O_Y. Its composite with the underlying abelian-sheaf functor is unchanged, so exactness and reflection of isomorphisms follow from the corresponding forgetful functor properties. The right-derived composition and exact-functor comparisons identify this restriction of Rg_*K with Rf_*K, without changing the original derived-category universes.

The affine unbounded cohomology formula gives H^i(Rf_*K)=f_*H^i(K). Retain the f_*O_X action on the same pushed K-injective complex, obtaining H^i(Rg_*K)=g_*H^i(K). On affine opens the comparison is algebra-linear; its maps commute with restriction and hence glue. Exact P gives H^i(D(P)(Rg_*K))=P(g_*H^i(K)). These comparisons are natural, and use the unbounded cohomological bound in the proof of the affine formula rather than claiming exactness of arbitrary direct image.

Compute the canonical derived counit on a K-injective resolution of K. The derived-adjunction counit equation makes it the ordinary counit after the right-derived comparison and the exact pullback comparison. Applying cohomology and the kernel/image comparisons of Step 2 identifies this with P(g_*H^i(K))→H^i(K). On affine opens its map sends b tensor s to b*s; compatibility with restrictions identifies it with the ordinary affine module counit. This is the counit calculation in 0AVW, independent of any derived unit factorization.

For each i the ordinary counit is invertible because H^i(K) is quasi-coherent. The homology comparisons in Step 2 therefore make H^i of the canonical derived counit invertible. The homology criterion for isomorphisms in the derived category proves its invertibility. Transport the underived adjunction from tensor pullback to the given a by uniqueness of left adjoints; the induced exact derived natural isomorphism transports the canonical counit. Empty schemes, zero modules and shifts satisfy the same argument.

theorem affine_algebra_exact_derived_counit_isIso
    {X Y : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings (directImageAlgebraSpace f)))]
    (P : SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings (directImageAlgebraSpace f)) ⥤
      SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    [P.Additive] [Limits.PreservesFiniteLimits P] [Limits.PreservesFiniteColimits P]
    (a : P ⊣ RingedSpace.moduleDirectImage (toDirectImageAlgebraSpace f))
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hK : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X K) :
    IsIso ((a.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction).counit.app K)
